description: Machine-checked routes from every tracked research report and GUI prototype to the governed specifications and decisions that consume it. reviewed_digest covers both sources and consumers so modifying either side requires an explicit cross-review.

routes.review_note: The research inventory and human traceability synthesis register all six owner-approved identity decisions, REV-C03-Q1 through Q6, REV-C04 standalone/offline and optional-Git integration, REV-C05 impact/reproducibility, and all REV-C06 Q1-Q6 amended/revised approvals. Q1 makes Navigator revision structure permanently visible; Q2 keeps one cohesive Release pane with persistent summaries; Q3 keeps summary and canonical witness tree simultaneously visible; Q4 keeps one complete Change hierarchy while profiles scale obligation and detail; Q5 keeps final atomic issuance in that pane through an exact-consequence arm-then-confirm bar; Q6 keeps verdicts and permanent counted manifest categories visible while opening immutable detail beside the summary. V9-A separates mutable Publish Sets from controlled issued records; V10-C establishes typed standing facts. Git and air-gap exchanges remain mapped, verified, quarantined adapter inputs. The split V1-V12 studies, distributed-collaboration re-entry, and unimplemented Global Preferences follow-ons remain linked; source-strength gates are preserved and no implementation is authorized.

The owner-directed Claude-only visual-truth lane is codified in AGENTS.md and enforced before rustfmt by the dependency-free staged-index checker. LANE-C02 owner approval governs the exact marker contract; tests cover refusal and exact-marker acceptance for adds/copies/modifications/mode changes/deletions and renames both directions, plus malformed markers and records, unusual filenames, hook ordering, fail-closed Git errors, and non-mutation. Codex remains forbidden from setting or forwarding the marker, and LANE-I01 changes no prototype file.
The historical focus/tab incident is retained against the native terminal interaction contract.

Material rendering and regression research constrain the Rendering Book and visual proof harness. Product Mechanics 036 changes only schematic theme selection, naming, and persistence; it preserves geometry, material colors, render fidelity, board palettes, and regression obligations.
Feedback proximity and Console research are reconciled with their guidance, shell specification, and ratified Console decision.
Compound semantics and visual language jointly constrain the universal selection contract.
Context-menu research feeds the content inventory and shell interaction specification.
The complete standards corpus is reviewed as one cross-domain input set against the standards specification and integration guidance.

The complete REV-C01 through REV-C07 evidence corpus was cross-reviewed into Product Mechanics 034 and the governed Product Revision Engine specification without widening the owner-ratified mechanism. The two-clock identity system, per-CI EngineeringRevision namespaces, immutable baseline composition, atomic affected-revision issuance, V9-A ControlledDocument chain, V10-C typed standing, standalone local authority, optional subordinate Git adapter, witness-backed impact, explicit library uptake, identity-aligned comparison, immutable regeneration, and byte-identical reproduction remain exact. The owner-reviewed enterprise posture is now explicit: external configuration managers may exercise scoped Datum Configuration/Release capability through RoleAssignment and signed attestation exchange, while Git/PLM/PDM/workflow systems remain subordinate adapters whose inbound material passes quarantine and whose outward role is mirroring; no external-master mode exists. REV-I10A makes assignment, bounded delegation, role-derived queues, authority visibility, and this external-manager workflow mandatory before production acceptance. REV-C06 Q1-Q6 retain their amended visual dispositions: permanent expanded Navigator structure, cohesive Release summaries with unresolved-collapse refusal, summary plus beside-opened witness tree, one profile-scaled Change hierarchy, in-pane arm-then-confirm issuance, and verdict-first counted evidence with beside-opened manifest. The corrected REV-C07 law applies non-blocking Design authoring to every profile that has not explicitly adopted earlier control and makes ignoring the revision engine a supported first-class workflow. Global Preferences now carries two named ratification-day owner requirements without changing engine truth: Hide Revision System remains a user right when unmanaged, while typed managed policy may pin visibility on with disclosed provenance; and the first Release is a specified accessible onboarding moment rather than an accidental encounter. REV-C08 places the bounded REV-I00 through REV-I12 implementation and proof sequence without authorizing execution: Global Preferences policy resolution and an explicit owner gate precede engine work, and Publish remains blocked through production acceptance. The owner-approved GP-C01 internal audit proves that Datum has only one Console-owned persisted UI value, independent launch/environment controls, session-only GUI state, and separate Project/domain authority; it also proves that no unified precedence/provenance/migration/recovery authority, managed Revision visibility, or first-Release onboarding state exists. GP-C02 adds primary-authority evidence for stable typed setting identity, distinct value-precedence and constraint-authority axes, provenance queries, config/state separation, durable generational persistence, unknown-field preservation, expected-generation mutation, explicit sync conflicts, accessible managed-state presentation, and controlled deviations. These are bounded requirement candidates for GP-C03 rather than an architecture, provider, dependency, or standards-conformance decision. The GP-C03 packet converts those findings into a dependency-ordered, one-question-at-a-time owner process. Q1-A establishes one stable PreferenceKey and one authoritative subsystem-owned descriptor. Q2-A establishes one resolver over typed source families and setting classes while keeping Project mutation, restartable/transient state, and explicit operation inputs outside the writable preference lattice. GP-C02B adds official SOLIDWORKS/PDM, Altium, Revit, and KiCad evidence for apply-once versus lock, standards-profile composition, selective portability, attributed administration, and explicit offline behavior; peer mechanisms remain non-normative and external services subordinate. Q3 adopts typed Recommend/Constrain/Pin/Lock directives gated by a typed, revocable, user-held AuthorityRelease; enrollment grants nothing, excess requests remain visible and inert, backside management is the expected enterprise posture, full management is explicitly released, accessibility carve-outs require descriptor justification, and governed-Project law remains independent. Q4 approves eligibility-before-control-before-value resolution, User over Recommendation over Installation over default, retention after Pin displacement, and typed conflict instead of last-writer wins. The owner-directed course correction makes preferences-window.html the working prototype and retains preferences-ux-study.html as archival structural evidence. The owner resumed Q5-Q10 one question at a time on 2026-08-27 under a binding primary-window visual-anchor law. Q5 extracts the rendered copy-once receipt behavior from #files-projects, #revision, #publish-space, and #units; alternatives that live-link Project policy or omit the receipt conflict with the drawn window, PM-035, Q1-Q4, and the Product Revision Engine copied-policy seam. The owner approved Q5-A on 2026-08-27, establishing immutable snapshot resolution, atomic Project-authority copy, a durable itemized receipt, and no live following without deciding profile origin or preview UX. The canvas-background decision remains the PM-036 precedent separating machine Presentation state from Project-policy seeds. The Claude-owned first-run, guided-setup, and Start-page studies are registered as clay source evidence. The prepared Q5A packet recommends guided-in-place B as the governing zero-mandatory-choice manual path with optional proposal-only C; A remains drawn comparative evidence. It extracts the static, no-jump focus treatment, non-blocking Skip/Esc behavior, keyboard and reduced-motion obligations, local completion/dismissal state, and the absence of replay/reset UI without authoring ahead of the prototypes. Q5B remains queued before existing Q6-Q10 with no Start-page disposition or clause. Profile origin and pre-creation preview do not change Q5's invariant copy semantics. The catalog remains clay except for separately owner-ratified boundaries. Product Mechanics 036 requires one persisted machine Presentation descriptor for complete Dark/Light schematic drawing themes, with Dark default, no free palette editing, and no effect on board or Publish output. A complete subsystem-wide V1 Preference Descriptor Catalog remains a named pre-ratification deliverable. Other persistence and final UX remain undecided. The GP-C01 through GP-C07 plan preserves that handoff before architecture decisions begin. Publish keeps composition and staleness presentation while consuming the one ConfigurationRef and Revision Engine facts. Licensed-text/source-strength, dependency-029, no-certification, no-multi-writer-merge, and no-Publish-implementation boundaries remain preserved. The complete route and the prototype-rendering-and-publish route were reviewed against all consumers; no prototype file changed, no consumer contradiction remains, and Q5/Q5A authorize no implementation or dependency.
Parametric editor and DXF research feed the library-authoring and footprint-system contracts.

Typography, clearance, text-engine, and manufacturing compaction research are jointly governed by the Rendering Book. Product Mechanics 036 preserves typography and clearance semantics while resolving schematic foreground roles through one selected contrast theme.
The product-mechanics research is retained against the controlling product doctrine.
Terminal state inventory and redesign research feed the native terminal contract and implementation plan.

Editor-shell and pane prototypes constrain the completed DOC-C04 Publish study alongside the shell, conformance, document/view, and pane-tiling authorities; the study extends rather than redesigns them.
The owner-disposed Console visual study remains paired with its decision and shell contract.
Context-menu visual authority and comparative open-fork evidence stay attached to the shell interaction contract.

The owner-approved DOC-C04 Publish Space visual contract is registered as one cross-linked three-file study: publish-space-study.html owns frames A-B and the complete OR-1..OR-8 index, publish-composition-study.html owns frames C-E, and publish-lifecycle-study.html owns frames F-H. The split preserves every frame anchor and ratified visual while restoring source-health; all cross-file index links resolve to the file owning their target. The contract remains integrated into specs/PUBLISH_SPACE_SPEC.md, including navigation, composition, Viewport state, revision-boundary presentation, and both type-first Pane titles. REV-C03-Q5 further clarifies that a Publish Set owns editable ordering and explicit source bindings only; separate ControlledDocuments, DocumentIssues, ReleasePackages, and Transmittals retain governed identity. Referenced-source deletion still refuses until dependencies are removed or retargeted. Product Mechanics 036 adds the owner-approved canvas study and makes Dark/Light authoring themes independent of Publish templates, render intent, and output.

The owner-reviewed selection visual study remains paired with functional and rendering authorities. Product Mechanics 036 changes the selected schematic contrast theme as a whole and does not weaken the locked non-color selection treatment or selection semantics.
The terminal visual study remains attached to the native terminal product contract.
